history.content:
Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().
CheckboxInput setting attrs['checked'] to True: ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/master/django/forms/widgets.py#L527

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().
CheckboxInput setting attrs['checked'] to True: ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/master/django/forms/widgets.py#L527

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().
CheckboxInput setting attrs['checked'] to True: ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/master/django/forms/widgets.py#L527

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. The root cause is visible: `final_attrs` is constructed once for the entire array and passed repeatedly to each subwidget. `CheckboxInput.get_context()` adds `checked` directly to that dictionary, so later checkboxes inherit it. I’ll create a standalone reproducer that inspects each subwidget’s rendered `checked` state before changing production code.

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().
CheckboxInput setting attrs['checked'] to True: ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/master/django/forms/widgets.py#L527

Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. The root cause is visible: `final_attrs` is constructed once for the entire array and passed repeatedly to each subwidget. `CheckboxInput.get_context()` adds `checked` directly to that dictionary, so later checkboxes inherit it. I’ll create a standalone reproducer that inspects each subwidget’s rendered `checked` state before changing production code.

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().
CheckboxInput setting attrs['checked'] to True: ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/master/django/forms/widgets.py#L527

Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. The root cause is visible: `final_attrs` is constructed once for the entire array and passed repeatedly to each subwidget. `CheckboxInput.get_context()` adds `checked` directly to that dictionary, so later checkboxes inherit it. I’ll create a standalone reproducer that inspects each subwidget’s rendered `checked` state before changing production code.

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().
CheckboxInput setting attrs['checked'] to True: ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/master/django/forms/widgets.py#L527

The root cause is visible: `final_attrs` is constructed once for the entire array and passed repeatedly to each subwidget. `CheckboxInput.get_context()` adds `checked` directly to that dictionary, so later checkboxes inherit it. I’ll create a standalone reproducer that inspects each subwidget’s rendered `checked` state before changing production code.

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().
CheckboxInput setting attrs['checked'] to True: ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/master/django/forms/widgets.py#L527

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().

The root cause is visible: `final_attrs` is constructed once for the entire array and passed repeatedly to each subwidget. `CheckboxInput.get_context()` adds `checked` directly to that dictionary, so later checkboxes inherit it. I’ll create a standalone reproducer that inspects each subwidget’s rendered `checked` state before changing production code.

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().
CheckboxInput setting attrs['checked'] to True: ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/master/django/forms/widgets.py#L527

The root cause is visible: `final_attrs` is constructed once for the entire array and passed repeatedly to each subwidget. `CheckboxInput.get_context()` adds `checked` directly to that dictionary, so later checkboxes inherit it. I’ll create a standalone reproducer that inspects each subwidget’s rendered `checked` state before changing production code.

import django

from django import forms
from django.contrib.postgres.forms import SplitArrayField

    context = field.widget.get_context('array', initial, attrs)
    return [
        (subwidget['name'], bool(subwidget['attrs'].get('checked')), dict(subwidget['attrs']))
        for subwidget in context['widget']['subwidgets']
    ]


for attrs in (None, {'id': 'id_array'}):
    print('attrs:', attrs)
    for row in checked_states([True, False, False, True, False], attrs):

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().
CheckboxInput setting attrs['checked'] to True: ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/master/django/forms/widgets.py#L527

The root cause is visible: `final_attrs` is constructed once for the entire array and passed repeatedly to each subwidget. `CheckboxInput.get_context()` adds `checked` directly to that dictionary, so later checkboxes inherit it. I’ll create a standalone reproducer that inspects each subwidget’s rendered `checked` state before changing production code.
